model_surface_schema.purpose: Per-harness record of the model-selection surface the harness documents for #434. Repo-side only; never installed. Every cell is stated — a missing feature is a finding, never a blank.

keys.enumeration: { available: bool, command: string, notes: string }
keys.identity: string — the naming SCHEME only; never a concrete model id
keys.runtime_model_override: { kind: per-spawn | static-agent-file | session-level | none, notes: string }
keys.effort: { kind: separate-key | folded-into-model-string | run-level | none, vocabulary: string, clamp: string, notes: string }
keys.declared_pool: { mechanism: string, enforcement: abort | warn | fallback | none, notes: string }
keys.reported_gaps: [{ item: string, label: reported-not-documented, url: string }]
keys.notes: string — must name the first-party URL the row was checked against

model_surface_schema.enumeration_rule: `enumeration.command` is non-empty if and only if `enumeration.available` is true — a blank command must never be read downstream as a usable pool.

enforcement_values.warn: The harness reports the identity but proceeds
enforcement_values.fallback: The harness substitutes a different model; the audit line records `substituted`
enforcement_values.none: No native mechanism exists, so the orchestrator self-enforces or falls to `inherit`

model_surface_schema.axis: This record asserts TARGET CAPABILITY — what the harness documents — not what our adapter emits. That is a different axis from the CI-enforced `agents` and `effort` flags, which assert EMISSION: a harness can document an effort surface and still be `effort: false` because the adapter emits no key.
model_surface_schema.sibling_relationship: #296 owns neutral spawn-hint RENDERING and consumes this record, including its `runtime_model_override` sub-key; #434 owns the record itself. One record, one owner — #296 must not add a second.

runtime_verified_schema.purpose: Per-harness record of whether Shipmates has been exercised against a running harness (#497). Repo-side only; never installed. Every cell is stated — unknown is a finding, never a blank. Distinct from format/digest verification and from the agents/effort emission flags.

keys.status: full | partial | none — full = crew_resolve is yes|n/a AND argument_passing=yes AND command_e2e=yes with at least one command named; partial = a live run is recorded but at least one criterion is unknown or no; none = no live run recorded
keys.verified_on: YYYY-MM-DD, or empty string when status is none
keys.crew_resolve: yes | no | n/a | unknown — n/a when the adapter ships skills-only (no crew to resolve)
keys.command_e2e: yes | no | unknown — whether a named command completed end to end on that harness
keys.commands_exercised: [string] — command names proven end-to-end; empty when unknown or none
keys.notes: string — evidence source (issue, date); never promote an unknown cell to yes

runtime_verified_schema.status_rule: `status` is full only when crew_resolve∈{yes,n/a}, argument_passing=yes, command_e2e=yes, commands_exercised is non-empty, and verified_on is a date. status is none only when verified_on is empty and commands_exercised is empty. Otherwise status is partial.
runtime_verified_schema.axis: This record asserts LIVE RUNTIME evidence — what was actually run — not payload format checks. Format/digest verification lives in agents_notes and CI digests; model-selection surfaces live in model_surface.

pi.agents_notes: NOTE THE DEPENDENCY: pi's subagent mechanic is NOT in core pi — it comes from the third-party `pi-subagents` extension (github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents), and an install without it resolves no crew. With it, crew are pi-native at `.pi/agents/<name>.md` — the extension's canonical project scope, alongside `~/.pi/agent/agents/**/*.md` for user scope. `tools` must be a COMMA-SEPARATED SCALAR, never a YAML list: the reader is a line-based parser that opens a block on an empty value and reads the whole list as one unmatchable name, so a mismatched file leaves the seat with NO tools and no error — that was #437, where Antigravity's crew at the shared legacy `.agents/agents/` (which pi still reads for compatibility) was handed to pi. Shipmates emits to `.pi/agents/`, which outranks the legacy `.agents/` tree within whichever directory pi resolves as its project root (the nearest ancestor carrying `.pi/` or `.agents/`). A project-local install therefore resolves correctly; a `--global` install resolves only when no nearer ancestor carries either, and pi's user scope cannot outrank a foreign `~/.agents/agents/` because legacy is loaded last. Verified 2026-09-13 against the extension's own source and docs.
pi.effort_notes: Per-agent `thinking:` frontmatter, applied at spawn as a `:<level>` model suffix. The accepted set is first-party in pi-subagents' own source — off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh — so the neutral low|medium|high passes through unclamped and unmapped. Unvalidated on parse, so an invented level would reach the model string and fail the spawn. Verified 2026-09-13.

effort.notes: A per-agent thinking key, a per-task override, a session flag, a settings default, per-model level maps and a budget map; a level can also ride the model argument as a suffix, and the resolved level is surfaced read-only to shell tools.
